children: Crude-sensitive stocks came under pressure on Tuesday as Brent oil prices surged towards the $100-a-barrel mark amid escalating tensions in the Middle East, raising concerns over higher input costs and inflationary pressures for several Indian companies. Oil marketing companies (OMCs), tyre makers and paint stocks were among those trading lower, while upstream producers Oil India and ONGC gained as rising crude prices improved the outlook for oil realisations.

Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) shares were down 2.88 percent at Rs 303.90 in afternoon trade, while Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) fell 2.42 percent to Rs 348.25. Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) declined 0.92 percent to Rs 133.90.

The weakness in OMC stocks came as Brent crude futures jumped more than 2 percent to around $99 a barrel, having touched $99.22 earlier in the session, their highest level since July 24. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude climbed more than 3 percent to around $94.4 a barrel.

Oil prices surged after Iran-backed Houthis attacked Saudi energy facilities, forcing operations at some facilities to be halted. Meanwhile, Iran threatened the US with "economic warfare", adding to concerns over further escalation and disruption to energy supplies and shipping in the Middle East.

Tyre, paint stocks decline on higher crude concerns

Tyre stocks also fell as higher crude prices raised concerns over raw-material costs. Apollo Tyres was down 2.20 percent at Rs 411.55, JK Tyre & Industries declined 1.07 percent to Rs 364.50, while CEAT slipped 0.83 percent to Rs 3,308.40. Crude oil and its derivatives are important inputs for tyre manufacturers, meaning a sustained rise in oil prices can put pressure on raw-material costs and margins unless companies are able to pass the increase on through higher prices.

Paint stocks traded lower as well. Berger Paints India declined 0.80 percent to Rs 480.60, Kansai Nerolac Paints fell 0.44 percent to Rs 193.42 and Asian Paints was down 0.26 percent at Rs 2,494.30. However, aviation stocks were relatively resilient despite the sharp increase in crude prices. InterGlobe Aviation, which operates IndiGo, was marginally higher at Rs 5,001.50, while SpiceJet was flat at Rs 9.59.
ONGC, Oil India gain as crude prices rise

The impact was reversed for upstream oil producers, which typically benefit from higher crude realisations. Oil India shares jumped 2.02 percent to Rs 496.85, while ONGC gained 1.19 percent to Rs 236.47.

Goldman Sachs has raised its longer-term oil-price forecasts, increasing its December 2026 forecasts for Brent and WTI by $5 to $85 and $80 a barrel, respectively. It raised its 2027 forecasts to $80 for Brent and $75 for WTI, based on an assumption that Middle East shipping disruptions will persist into next year.

The spike in crude prices weighed on the broader Indian market as well. At 2:51 pm, the Sensex was down 535 points, or 0.70 percent, at 75,597, while the Nifty 50 fell 137 points, or 0.58 percent, to 23,642. The Nifty Oil & Gas index was down 0.76 percent.

title: Crude-sensitive stocks fall as Brent crude jumps past $100; BPCL, HPCL, Apollo Tyres drop, oil producers gain
